lead: BRS recycles your used, broken or obsolete computers and CPUs, with data destruction and reuse considered before anything is dismantled.
card_blurb: Recycling of used, broken or obsolete business computers, with data wiped or destroyed first.
meta_description: BRS recycles used, broken or obsolete business computers and CPUs, with secure data destruction and reuse options before disassembly.
overview: Office desktops, workstations and business PCs are classed as e-waste and need to be recycled properly. BRS recycles your used, broken or obsolete computers and CPUs.
Our customers are mostly companies upgrading their systems. They call us to take the older hardware off their hands.

benefits.title: Responsible disposal
benefits.text: Computers are kept out of landfills and handled as e-waste.

benefits.title: Data stays protected
benefits.text: Hard drives are wiped or destroyed before anything else happens.

benefits.title: Reuse where possible
benefits.text: Working computers can be donated, and others are dismantled for parts.

included: Data destruction by wiping or destroying hard drives
Recycling of CPUs and business PCs

process.title: Collect hardware
process.text: We collect the unwanted computers your company no longer needs.

process.title: Destroy data
process.text: Hard drives are wiped or destroyed so data cannot be recovered.

process.title: Test for reuse
process.text: Working computers are identified for donation or reuse.

process.title: Disassemble and sort
process.text: Remaining units are taken apart and materials sorted for recycling.

who_for: Offices with used or broken PCs and CPUs
Businesses that need data destroyed on old hard drives
Organizations that want working computers reused

faq.a: E-waste, or electronic waste, describes used electronics nearing the end of their useful life that are discarded, donated or given to a recycler.

faq.q: What happens to the data on our computers?
faq.a: Deleting files does not remove data, so hard drives are wiped or destroyed to prevent leaks.

faq.q: What happens to computers that still work?
faq.a: Working computers are tested for reuse and can be donated. Others are dismantled and sorted for recycling.
